acceptance.given: A validator invocation is made through the public Python or CLI entry using malformed JSON, an unreadable or out-of-root target, duplicate JSON keys, or an unsupported contract version; separately, identical bytes and policy are supplied to two runs.

oracle.expected: Each invalid input or target case returns a non-pass structured result with applicable bounded diagnostics and outcome-consistent exit semantics. Repeated runs over identical bytes and policy yield equivalent sorted structured output without timestamps or environment-secret values.
forbidden: Any listed invalid input or target condition returns pass.
Repeated equivalent runs differ materially or return unsorted equivalent diagnostics.
Output includes timestamps, environment-secret values, absolute host paths, or arbitrary source text.
oracle.observable: During direct Python API and CLI execution, compare the structured result, status, exit code, ordered diagnostics and serialized output across the specified invalid cases and repeated identical runs.

acceptance.then: Each invalid case produces a non-pass result with bounded applicable diagnostics and correct exit semantics, while identical repeated runs produce equivalent sorted output without timestamps or environment-secret values.
acceptance.when: Invoke the real validator entry for each invalid case and for two runs over identical bytes and policy; inspect and compare the structured results and CLI exit behavior.

Validate with python -B -m pytest scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_core.py::test_a06 -q (timeout 300 seconds).
